description: This radial chart, titled “Task-wise Class Distributions” from the paper “A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource Settings,” visually represents the distribution of abusive and non-abusive language categories across different task types. The chart is structured as a multi-layered donut chart with “TiALD” at the center, radiating outwards into two primary concentric rings: “Abusive” (in teal) and “Not Abusive” (in yellow). The “Abusive” ring is further divided into categories such as “Political,” “Racial,” “Sexist,” “Religious,” “Other,” and “Mixed,” each of which is subdivided into sentiment classes labeled “Negative,” “Positive,” “Neutral,” or “Mixed.” Similarly, the “Not Abusive” ring is segmented into “Positive,” “Neutral,” “Negative,” “Mixed,” and “Other,” each with their own subcategories. The “Abusive” ring is visually dominant, occupying the majority of the chart’s area, suggesting that abusive instances are more prevalent than non-abusive ones. The chart includes a legend that maps the color coding to the sentiment classes (Negative, Positive, Neutral, Mixed), although the legend is not fully visible in the image. The segments appear to be ordered by size, with the largest slice in the “Abusive” ring being “Other,” followed by “Political,” and the smallest being “Mixed.” The chart does not include percentage labels within the slices, but the relative sizes clearly indicate the proportion of each category.
